To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Draft handover for Thursday’s launch

DRAFT — for Inês to review before sharing

Inês,

Thank you for taking this on at short notice. I’m sorry I’m leaving you with extra work, especially after finding the figure 3 error so late. The mistake is mine, not yours. You know this paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity work yourself. I trust you completely to lead the launch and handle the questions. You’re better live than you think: I still remember how you rescued my panel in Lisbon when the projector died. You’ve got this.

I’m travelling tonight because my father is ill, and I’m with my family. I may not be reachable after 09:00 tomorrow. You can call me, but please don’t wait for me to move anything forward.

Suggested order

1. First thing tomorrow: confirm the revised schedule and responsibilities with Tomás and Hanna. The MEP’s vote means the presentation is now 15 minutes and the panel should start at 12:50. The original run of show has a 12:30 welcome and a 12:35 presentation, so check the precise revised timings and who will manage the questions before the MEP leaves at 13:30. She wants to take at least two questions herself. The original schedule has Q&A at 13:40, which no longer fits; don’t rely on it without confirmation. Ask Tomás to confirm the final sequence, the room, and any practical requirements. Guests need to be at the security entrance by 12:00, and Tomás is collecting badges.

2. By Wednesday at 12:00, send Tomás the final names for anyone attending from our side. He says security will not admit them without the list. Please check names with the team rather than assuming the existing list is complete.

3. Correct the launch materials before they are used. The corrected PDF v7 is on the drive; it updates pages 3, 14 and 15. The figure and summary should give the 2030 LDC-relevant revenue as EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The old number came from a run that did not apply the free-allocation phase-out. Please update deck v4, especially slides 6 and 9, and check the speaker notes and any other copies of the chart. Inês, you made the deck shorter and noted that slide 9 has the revenue chart; the error is mine, not yours. The paper’s conclusion does not change, but the headline number does. Use the corrected PDF as the source of truth and check every version before the event.

4. Coordinate the press-release correction with Hanna as soon as possible, and make sure it is addressed before the embargo lifts at 10:00 CET on Thursday. The release sent to 34 Brussels contacts on Friday still says EUR 2.1 billion. Please agree with Hanna how to correct it and notify the recipients clearly; don’t let the old figure go live uncorrected. If Hanna wants a senior name to sign off a corrected release, Geert can do that. He knows I’m away. The two background calls are in the calendar for Wednesday at 14:00 and 15:00, 20 minutes each; Hanna was due to confirm them. Please coordinate who will take them and make sure the corrected figure is used in any call or follow-up. If asked directly about the error, say plainly that the 2.1 figure was my mistake. Don’t leave Hanna to explain it as your error.

5. For Kessler’s likely panel challenge, keep the answer calm and evidence-led. He has raised the 80% pass-through assumption and resource shuffling. The 80% is our central case; annex B tests 40% and 60%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%, so acknowledge that range openly rather than getting defensive or presenting the central case as universal. He may try to make the whole discussion about the 80%. Don’t let him set the tone: explain what the sensitivity runs show, then bring the conversation back to the paper’s broader findings and the implications for LDCs. On resource shuffling, acknowledge the risk, point to section 5.2, and note our recommendation for the Commission’s monitoring report. Abena was strong on the LDC side in our call and may add useful perspective, but don’t depend on her to answer for us. Her remote link was tested and works.

6. On Thursday, arrive with time to check the room, slides, remote connection and corrected press materials. The lunch is outside the room from 12:00. Tomás is handling badges; check that the final deck is the corrected version and that the remote connection for Abena is ready. Keep the shortened 14-slide deck and revised timings in view. If the projector or connection fails, pause, speak to the room, and use the PDF or another practical fallback rather than letting the technical issue take over. You’ve handled that kind of moment before.

7. After the launch, please follow up with Lucy Tran from Halvorsen Foundation: she and a colleague are attending and need two event photos and attendance numbers for their grant report, ideally by 4 December. Arrange for someone to take and keep suitable photos, and confirm the attendance count while it’s available. You can send the follow-up once the event is over; it doesn’t need to distract from the launch itself.

I’m sorry I can’t be there, and I’m sorry about the last-minute correction. I know how much work you’ve put into this, and I trust you to make the event clear, honest and composed. Thank you for stepping in.
